title: Count Orders Per Customer Without GROUP BY
description:
Show each order along with the total number of orders that customer has placed — without collapsing rows using GROUP BY.

**Table: orders** — `order_id`, `customer_id`, `order_date`, `amount`

Output columns: `order_id`, `customer_id`, `order_date`, `amount`, `customer_order_count`. Order by `customer_id`, `order_date`.
solution_sql: SELECT order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS customer_order_count FROM orders ORDER BY customer_id, order_date

test_cases.description: 9 orders for 3 customers: customer 101 has 3 orders, 102 has 2, 103 has 4

hints: COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) counts all rows in the partition without ORDER BY, giving the total per customer for every row.
This keeps all individual rows (unlike GROUP BY) while still showing the aggregate count alongside each order.
explanation: COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) is a non-aggregating aggregate — it returns the count for each partition without collapsing rows. Customer 101 has 3 orders so all 3 of their rows show customer_order_count=3. Customer 102 shows 2 on both rows. Customer 103 shows 4 on all four rows. This is invaluable when row-level detail and partition-level aggregates are needed in one query.
